trials.notes: Exact documented pattern: WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), next_tag('A'), get_attribute() with is_string(), a depth-bounded next_token() walk, #text filtering, and get_modifiable_text(). No _doing_it_wrong records.

Same correct documented pattern as trial-1. The extra paused_at_incomplete_token() break is documented and harmless here, but slightly over-specifies an incomplete-input policy for a read-only extractor.

Uses documented APIs correctly, including array next_tag query and is_tag_closer(). The closer guard is redundant because next_tag() skips closers by default unless tag_closers => 'visit' is requested.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial; all executions passed 8/8 with no _doing_it_wrong records. The docs worked well here: 'Which processor should I use?' directs text/subtree work to WP_HTML_Processor; 'Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree', next_token(), and get_current_depth() show the exact depth-bounded #text-token walk; get_modifiable_text() documents decoded text; get_attribute() documents null/true/string semantics; and the incomplete-input notes explain that read-only extraction policy is caller-defined. Near-misses were minor: trial-2 showed uncertainty about whether to stop on paused_at_incomplete_token(), and trial-3 showed uncertainty about next_tag()'s default opener-only behavior.

doc_gaps.problem: The HTML Processor method section shows true/null examples but does not repeat the Tag Processor note that returned string values are already decoded.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add the decoded-string contract directly to WP_HTML_Processor::get_attribute(), with a reminder not to decode again.

doc_gaps.problem: The phrase 'Boolean attributes return true' can be read as spec-defined boolean attributes only, while valueless attributes such as href also return true.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Clarify that any present attribute written without a value returns true, and recommend is_string() when callers require an actual attribute value.

doc_gaps.problem: The default tag_closers => 'skip' behavior is only in the parameter table; one trial still added an unnecessary closer guard.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short prose note or example immediately under next_tag(): plain next_tag() and next_tag('A') visit openers only; use tag_closers => 'visit' when closers are needed.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs say completion policy is caller-defined, but do not clearly contrast unclosed elements that still yield virtual closers with truly incomplete syntax that pauses parsing.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a small general example showing best-effort read-only extraction from an unclosed element versus a truncated syntax token, and when paused_at_incomplete_token() should affect the result.
